pending_diagnosis: DIAGNOSIS: Anti-NMDA Receptor Encephalitis (secondary to an Ovarian Teratoma) THE SMOKING GUN: Pelvic ultrasound revealing a 4 cm ovarian mature cystic teratoma (dermoid cyst) containing ectopic neural tissue, paired with positive anti-GluN1 IgG antibodies in the cerebrospinal fluid. PATHOPHYSIOLOGY: The underlying benign ovarian teratoma contains expressed neural tissue, triggering an autoimmune response. The patient produces cross-reactive IgG autoantibodies against the extracellular GluN1 subunit of N-methyl-D-aspartate (NMDA) receptors. These autoantibodies cross the blood-brain barrier and bind to presynaptic GABAergic interneurons in the central nervous system, causing cross-linking and internalizing of NMDA receptors. This loss of inhibitory control leads to frontostriatal hyper-dopaminergic disinhibition, driving the classic sequence of acute psychosis, movement disorders, seizures, autonomic instability, and central hypoventilation. Treatment requires urgent surgical resection of the teratoma combined with immunomodulatory therapies (plasmapheresis, IVIG, and corticosteroids).
